name: Murray v. UBS Securities, LLC
holding: Under SOX Section 1514A, a whistleblower-plaintiff must prove that retaliatory intent was a contributing factor in the adverse action, and need not prove the employer acted with the specific intent to retaliate. The plaintiff's burden requires showing protected activity was a contributing factor, not the sole cause.
ai_relevance: Sets the causation standard for SOX whistleblower retaliation claims, directly relevant to AI safety whistleblowers at publicly traded companies.

name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc. v. Somers
holding: The Dodd-Frank Act's anti-retaliation provision protects only whistleblowers who report to the SEC, not those who report internally or to other agencies. Employees reporting internally are not covered by Dodd-Frank's retaliation cause of action.
ai_relevance: Defines the boundary of Dodd-Frank whistleblower protection: internal reporters at AI companies lack a private retaliation claim under Dodd-Frank.

name: Lawson v. FMR LLC
holding: SOX Section 1514A whistleblower protection extends to employees of private contractors and subcontractors who work for publicly traded companies, even if the employee works for a private firm.
ai_relevance: Extends SOX protection to contractor employees — relevant to the many private AI labs and contractors serving public companies.

court: US District Court, Southern District of California
name: Erhart v. BOFI Federal Bank
holding: An IRS whistleblower who files suit waives attorney-client and work-product privilege as to the subject matter of the whistleblower claim; the court also set standards for IRS whistleblower retaliation litigation.
ai_relevance: Illustrates the litigation consequences whistleblowers face — privilege waiver — relevant to internal AI safety reporters weighing disclosure.

name: United States ex rel. Polansky v. Executive Health Resources, Inc.
holding: The government may dismiss a False Claims Act qui tam action over the relator's objection; the court sets the standard for such dismissal motions, balancing the government's interests.
ai_relevance: Relevant to FCA theories applied to AI-related claims submitted to government programs (e.g., billing fraud with AI assistance).

name: In re Caremark International Inc. Derivative Litigation
holding: Corporate directors have an oversight duty to ensure reasonable information and reporting systems exist; liability for oversight failures requires a sustained or systematic failure to exercise oversight, now the Caremark standard.
ai_relevance: Foundational for board liability over AI safety oversight failures — the standard invoked in debates about director duties for AI governance.

name: Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
holding: Trial judges must act as gatekeepers for expert testimony, assessing relevance and reliability under Rule 702, including testability, error rates, and peer review. Replaced the Frye general-acceptance standard.
ai_relevance: The standard for admitting AI-derived expert evidence and algorithmic analyses in court; central to litigating AI evaluation results.

name: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo
holding: Overruled Chevron deference: courts must exercise independent judgment in interpreting statutes and may not defer to agency interpretations merely because a statute is ambiguous.
ai_relevance: Major shift for AI regulation: agencies (FTC, SEC, NLRB) can no longer rely on Chevron deference for statutory interpretation, affecting the pace and shape of AI rulemaking.

court: US District Court, Southern District of New York
name: Mata v. Avianca, Inc.
holding: Court sanctioned attorneys for submitting briefs containing six fabricated case citations generated by ChatGPT; emphasized counsel's duty to verify AI-generated legal research.
ai_relevance: First high-profile judicial sanction for AI-hallucinated citations; establishes professional-responsibility risks of AI research tools.

court: US District Court, Northern District of California
name: United States v. Holmes
holding: Elizabeth Holmes convicted of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud for misleading investors about Theranos technology capabilities; jury found false statements about device accuracy and revenue claims.
ai_relevance: Model for prosecuting misleading capability claims about technology — directly relevant to overstated AI performance claims in fundraising and sales.

name: Gonzalez v. Google LLC
holding: Court declined to decide whether Section 230 immunity covers algorithmic recommendations, holding the specific claims failed; left the scope of Section 230 for algorithmic content largely unresolved.
ai_relevance: Keeps open the question of platform immunity for AI-generated and algorithmically recommended content; central to AI content liability.
